preconditions.expression: all(c in '01' for c in stdin.splitlines()[0])
preconditions.description: The first line of stdin is a single integer T (1 ≤ T ≤ 100), followed by T test cases. Each test case is a single line containing a string S of length 1 ≤ |S| ≤ 10^5, where each character is either '0' or '1'.
The first line of stdin is parsed as an integer T, representing the number of test cases.
Each of the T test cases has a non-empty string S representing the initial card configuration.

postconditions.expression: stdout == '\n'.join(['WIN' if can_win(S) else 'LOSE' for S in stdin.splitlines()[1:T+1]]) + '\n'
postconditions.description: For each test case string S, the output line is 'WIN' if and only if Chef can remove all cards following the game rules, and 'LOSE' otherwise. The function can_win(S) determines this by checking if a valid sequence of moves exists to remove all cards.
Each output line for a test case is exactly 3 characters long ('WIN' or 'LOSE').
